first.rationale: Current situation shows simultaneous declines in activation (6% QoQ) and onboarding completion (4% QoQ), with competitive pressure on price-sensitive segments. Memory 91 directly addresses activation lift through in-product messaging, while memory 86 shows onboarding simplification works. Before committing, I'm verifying both to confirm the magnitude and durability of these effects. Activation messaging is the highest-leverage option because: (1) it directly targets the measured 6% activation decline, (2) it doesn't require pricing concessions that could undermine LTV in competitive dynamics, (3) it complements the prior onboarding work (memory 86) by improving post-signup engagement, and (4) it's faster to deploy than structural onboarding changes. The referral approach (memory 57) works best with established customers, which doesn't match our current acquisition-pressure moment. Enterprise sales assist (memory 44) is valuable but doesn't address the SMB activation leakage. Promotional pricing (memory 73) is a defensible fallback if verification reveals messaging had narrow applicability, but it risks margin compression during competitive incursion. Running activation_messaging as a standard_experiment lets us validate whether the prior lift persists in current conditions before broader rollout.

final.rationale: Verification confirms both prior experiments hold. Memory 86 showed +13% onboarding completion and +3% retention; memory 91 showed +6% activation lift with +11% week-one engagement and +1% retention. Current QoQ decline in activation (-6%) and onboarding completion (-4%) suggests these levers have degraded or conditions have shifted. Activation messaging is the optimal choice because: (1) it directly counteracts the measured 6% activation decline and aligns with verified +6% lift from exp_91, (2) the +11% week-one engagement lift compounds with memory 86's onboarding gains, creating synergy across the signup-to-activation funnel, (3) it avoids promotional pricing concessions during competitor entry—preserving margin and preventing a race-to-bottom on SMB revenue quality, (4) retention impact (+1%) is additive without cannibalizing higher-LTV cohorts, and (5) it's deployable within the week. The 4% onboarding completion decline could also benefit from re-running memory 86 simplification, but messaging is the higher-confidence near-term lever given the larger activation gap. This experiment preserves optionality: if activation_messaging underperforms in current conditions, we retain promotional_pricing as a Q4 lever and can revisit onboarding simplification with fresh data.
